scenarios.title: Checkout is crash-looping

alert.name: order-service pod restarts > 3 in 10m
alert.summary: order-service restarted 7 times in 10 minutes. Customers can't check out.

evidence.title: Pod restarts
evidence.query:
KubePodInventory
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30m) and Namespace == "pets"
| where ControllerName startswith "order-service"
| summarize Restarts = max(ContainerRestartCount) by Name, ContainerStatusReason
evidence.output:
Name                            ContainerStatusReason  Restarts
order-service-7c9d8f6b4-2xkqp   CrashLoopBackOff       7
order-service-7c9d8f6b4-m8z4w   CrashLoopBackOff       6
evidence.finding: Both replicas are crash-looping, so this isn't one bad pod or node.

evidence.title: Last container state
evidence.output:
...
    Last State:     Terminated
      Reason:       OOMKilled
      Exit Code:    137
    Limits:
      memory:  16Mi
    Requests:
      memory:  8Mi
...
evidence.finding: Exit code 137 with reason OOMKilled: the kernel killed the container for exceeding its 16Mi memory limit.

evidence.title: Container memory
evidence.query:
Perf
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30m)
| where ObjectName == "K8SContainer" and CounterName == "memoryWorkingSetBytes"
| where InstanceName endswith "/order-service"
| summarize PeakMiB = max(CounterValue) / 1048576 by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
evidence.finding: Working set hits the 16Mi limit within seconds of every start. There's no slow climb, so this isn't a leak.

evidence.title: order-service logs
evidence.query:
ContainerLogV2
| where PodNamespace == "pets" and ContainerName == "order-service"
| project TimeGenerated, LogMessage
| take 3
evidence.output:
09:41:02  Listening on port 3000
09:41:02  Connecting to rabbitmq:5672
09:41:03  Connected to rabbitmq
evidence.finding: Logs stop with no error. That's typical when a process is killed from outside instead of crashing.

evidence.title: Node memory
evidence.finding: Nodes have plenty of free memory, so node pressure isn't evicting pods.

rootCauses.label: The container memory limit (16Mi) is far below what order-service needs
A memory leak in a recent order-service build
Node memory pressure is evicting pods
order-service can't reach RabbitMQ and exits

mitigations.label: Raise the order-service memory request and limit
mitigations.risk: Recreates order-service pods (brief downtime with the Recreate strategy).
mitigations.outcome: Pods start, working set settles near 48MiB, and restarts stop.

mitigations.label: Reapply the sandbox baseline manifest
mitigations.risk: Resets every pets workload to its known-good spec.
mitigations.outcome: order-service returns to its baseline limits and stops restarting.

mitigations.label: Restart the order-service pods
mitigations.outcome: New pods are OOMKilled again within 30 seconds. A restart treats the symptom.

mitigations.label: Scale order-service to 6 replicas
mitigations.risk: Adds 4 pods to the user node pool.
mitigations.outcome: Six pods crash-loop instead of two. More replicas don't give each pod more memory.

scenarios.lesson: Exit code 137, reason OOMKilled, and a working set pinned at the limit mean the limit is too low. Size requests and limits from observed usage.

learn.title: Resource management best practices for AKS

scenarios.title: Orders are never fulfilled

alert.name: makeline-service availability < 50%
alert.summary: Customers can place orders, but none has been fulfilled for 15 minutes. makeline-service is failing readiness checks.

evidence.title: makeline-service errors
evidence.query:
ContainerLogV2
| where PodNamespace == "pets" and ContainerName == "makeline-service"
| where LogMessage has "mongo"
| project TimeGenerated, LogMessage
| take 3
evidence.output:
09:58:12  failed to connect to mongodb://mongodb:27017: connection refused
09:58:42  failed to connect to mongodb://mongodb:27017: connection refused
09:59:12  readiness check failed: database unavailable
evidence.finding: makeline-service fails because it can't reach MongoDB. It's a victim, not the cause.

evidence.title: Deployment status
evidence.output:
NAME               READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE
makeline-service   0/1     1            0
mongodb            0/0     0            0
order-service      2/2     2            2
product-service    1/1     1            1
rabbitmq           1/1     1            1
store-admin        1/1     1            1
store-front        1/1     1            1
evidence.finding: The mongodb Deployment wants 0 replicas. Nothing crashed it; it was scaled to zero.

evidence.title: MongoDB events
evidence.query:
KubeEvents
| where Namespace == "pets" and Name startswith "mongodb"
| project TimeGenerated, Reason, Message
evidence.output:
09:43:05  ScalingReplicaSet  Scaled down replica set mongodb-5d8f7c9b6 to 0 from 1
09:43:06  Killing            Stopping container mongodb
evidence.finding: The scale-down event lines up with when fulfilment stopped.

evidence.title: Order queue
evidence.query: kubectl exec -n pets deploy/rabbitmq -- rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages
evidence.finding: Orders pile up in RabbitMQ, so order intake still works. The break is downstream.

evidence.title: order-service pods
evidence.output:
NAME                            READY   STATUS    RESTARTS
order-service-6f7b9c8d5-4hjkl   1/1     Running   0
order-service-6f7b9c8d5-p2xzq   1/1     Running   0
evidence.finding: order-service is healthy; it only publishes orders to RabbitMQ.

rootCauses.label: MongoDB was scaled to 0 replicas, so makeline-service lost its database
A bug in makeline-service makes it fail readiness checks
RabbitMQ is overloaded and dropping orders

mitigations.label: Scale MongoDB back to 1 replica
mitigations.risk: Starts MongoDB and reattaches its PersistentVolumeClaim.
mitigations.outcome: mongodb is 1/1 Ready. makeline-service reconnects and drains the 412 queued orders.

mitigations.label: Reapply the sandbox baseline manifest
mitigations.risk: Resets every pets workload to its known-good spec.
mitigations.outcome: MongoDB returns to 1 replica and makeline-service drains the queue.

mitigations.label: Restart makeline-service
mitigations.outcome: makeline-service fails readiness again. MongoDB is still at 0 replicas.

mitigations.label: Purge the orders queue to clear the backlog
mitigations.command: kubectl exec -n pets deploy/rabbitmq -- rabbitmqctl purge_queue orders
mitigations.outcome: You deleted 412 customer orders and makeline-service is still down. Never destroy data to quiet an alert.

scenarios.lesson: Follow the dependency chain before you act. The loudest service is often a victim of something further down.

scenarios.title: Orders fail, but every pod is green

alert.name: Order placement failure rate > 20%
alert.summary: Most POST /api/orders requests from store-front fail. No pods are restarting.

evidence.title: Pod health
evidence.query:
KubePodInventory
| where TimeGenerated > ago(15m) and Namespace == "pets"
| summarize Restarts = max(ContainerRestartCount) by ControllerName, PodStatus
evidence.output:
ControllerName      PodStatus  Restarts
store-front         Running    0
order-service       Running    0
product-service     Running    0
makeline-service    Running    0
rabbitmq            Running    0
mongodb             Running    0
evidence.finding: Every pod is Running with zero restarts. The fault isn't inside a container.

evidence.title: store-front proxy errors
evidence.query:
ContainerLogV2
| where PodNamespace == "pets" and ContainerName == "store-front"
| where LogMessage has "order-service"
| project TimeGenerated, LogMessage
| take 2
evidence.output:
10:12:40  connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, upstream: "http://order-service:3000/order"
10:12:44  connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream, upstream: "http://order-service:3000/order"
evidence.finding: store-front can resolve order-service, but nothing accepts the connection.

evidence.title: order-service Service
evidence.output:
Name:         order-service
Namespace:    pets
Selector:     app=order-service-v2
Type:         ClusterIP
Port:         <unset>  3000/TCP
TargetPort:   3000/TCP
Endpoints:    <none>
evidence.finding: The Service has no endpoints, and it selects app=order-service-v2.

evidence.title: order-service pod labels
evidence.output:
NAME                            READY   STATUS    LABELS
order-service-6f7b9c8d5-4hjkl   1/1     Running   app=order-service,pod-template-hash=6f7b9c8d5
order-service-6f7b9c8d5-p2xzq   1/1     Running   app=order-service,pod-template-hash=6f7b9c8d5
evidence.finding: The pods are labeled app=order-service. The Service selector matches none of them.

evidence.title: Network policies
evidence.output: No resources found in pets namespace.
evidence.finding: No NetworkPolicy exists, so policy isn't blocking traffic.

rootCauses.label: The order-service Service selector doesn't match the pod labels

mitigations.label: Point the Service selector back at app=order-service
mitigations.risk: Low. Only changes which pods the Service routes to.
mitigations.outcome: Endpoints fill with 2 pod IPs and order failures drop to 0%.

mitigations.label: Reapply the sandbox baseline manifest
mitigations.risk: Resets every pets workload to its known-good spec.
mitigations.outcome: The Service selector returns to app=order-service and orders flow again.

mitigations.label: Restart order-service
mitigations.outcome: New pods get the same labels. The Service still selects nothing and orders keep failing.

mitigations.label: Delete the order-service Service
mitigations.outcome: Now order-service doesn't resolve at all. You widened the outage.

scenarios.lesson: Healthy pods don't guarantee a healthy service. When pods are fine but traffic fails, compare Service selectors with pod labels and check endpoints.

learn.title: Network concepts for applications in AKS
